newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Telecoms still major part of CITIC Pac H1.
newsitem.headline: Telecoms still major part of CITIC Pac H1.

text.p: CITIC Pacific reaped the largest single portion of its earnings from its stake in Hong Kong Telecommunications Co Ltd, despite a significant reduction of that stake during the first half, according to the company's interim results announcement released on Tuesday.
However, investment in infrastructural development projects provided an increasing share of recurring profit.
The China-backed company reported first half profit of HK$4.99 million, including exceptional gains of HK$3.30 billion, up 255 percent over the year-earlier period.
In January and June CITIC Pacific disposed of a total of 3.85 percent of Hongkong Telecom, reducing its interest to approximately eight percent.
The telecom sector's contribution fell to 23 percent of total profit attributable to shareholders excluding exceptional gains during the period, from 28 percent, the report showed.
However, telecoms remains the single largest contributor to group earnings of the HK$1.69 billion in profit attributable to shareholders excluding exceptional gains.
The exceptional was due to the sale of the Hongkong Telecom shares and a 17.66 percent stake in Hong Kong Dragon Airlines.

The other major contributors to recurring profits were aviation and property investments. Those sectors both contributed 19 percent of group earnings compared to 19 and 21 percent respectively the previous year, the report said.

The group's investments in China -- power generation, roads and bridges, water purification facilities, and waste management projects in total contributed 21 percent of earnings in first half 1996, compared with 18 percent in the year-earlier period.
The company's strategy of increasing involvement in civil infrastructure on the mainland continued in the first half of 1996, the report said.

Contracts were signed for a 49 percent interest in 20-year franchises to operate eight existing water purification works in Nanjing and five existing works in Wuxi with a combined capacity of 2.7 million tonnes of water a day, the announcement said.
The company also acquired a 45 percent interest in a 20-year franchise to build and operate the Xu Pu bridge between Puxi and Pudong in Shanghai. -- Hong Kong newsroom (852) 2843 6933
